sun.upright:
Getting there first, and on your own, is how an Aries Sun likes to win. This is a card about getting there with other people and then stopping to mark it, and Aries isn't famous for either. The card is Mercury in Cancer, and Cancer squares Aries. Both are cardinal signs, both like to start things, and a square between them is friction that makes something happen. Put water on fire and you get steam, which is a fair description of what this draw does to you.

You'll probably recognise the pattern. You finish something, the launch or the race or the hard month, and before anyone's had a chance to say well done you're already looking at the next thing. Being toasted makes you twitchy. You say it was nothing, you change the subject, you buy the round so the moment's over. Some of that is modesty and some of it, to be honest, is that needing people feels like weakness to a Mars-ruled Sun. The card says the win belongs partly to the people who stood around you while you got it, and that letting them say so won't slow you down.

At work it's the project you drove through and the team who never got a drink out of it. With friends it's the mate you only ring when you need a hand moving house. With a brother or sister it can be the old competing, still going at forty, when what you both want is to be on the same side for once. Throw the small party for the thing you just finished. Invite the three people who helped, and let one of them give the speech.
sun.reversed:
When this card turns over for an Aries Sun, the company drops out and the competing stays. You go it alone out of pride and tell yourself it's quicker. Or the celebration itself turns into a contest, who's loudest at the table, who stays out latest, who tells the best version of the win. Mercury has no rank in Aries and falls in with Mars, so the talk gets quick and a bit combative, and the toast turns into a speech about you.

In a team it's the credit taken a beat too fast, and colleagues who've gone quiet around you. With friends it's a friendship that's become a scoreboard, who rang last, who owes whom. Often there's someone you fell out with over something small, and pride won't let you fix it. Ring them. Leave the argument out of it, ask how they are, and listen to the whole answer.

moon.upright:
Doing something is what settles an Aries Moon. A feeling turns up, you act on it, it's gone, and you'd honestly like everyone else to move on as quickly as you did. The Three of Cups offers a slower kind of comfort, being looked after by friends, talking it through over a drink, letting people make a fuss of you. The card's element is water and yours is fire, and those two either make steam or one puts the other out. Cancer and Aries are square as well, so there's no pretending this fit is easy.

Mercury in your sign picks up Mars's habits, which is why, when you do talk about how you feel, it comes out as a rant to your best friend in the car park, fast and funny and over in ten minutes. That counts for something. The trouble is the next bit, when your friend wants to stay with it and ask how you're really going, and you get fidgety and suggest going somewhere else. You like being the one who turns up with the energy. Being the one who gets cheered up is harder, and I've seen plenty of Aries Moons go years without letting a friend do it properly.

In friendships it's usually you who suggests the night out and rarely you who admits it's been a rough week. With a partner it's the quiet night in they wanted, and you pacing about in it. Your body is part of this too. Feelings move through you best when you're moving, so the running club, the netball team, the Saturday ride with a mate are where you'll feel held without having to sit still for it. Join the thing you'd do with a friend, and go every time.
moon.reversed:
Being left out lands hard on an Aries Moon, and with this card reversed it lands as anger first. You see the photos from the dinner you weren't asked to, and within a minute you've left the group chat or written something short and sharp in it. Mars rules your sign and Mercury takes its temper from him, so the words come out hot. Or it goes the other way and you pile into every night out to burn the feeling off, and come home more wound up than you left.

Old friendships take most of the damage, the ones with enough history for a hurt to catch on. Sleep suffers after the late nights. Before you leave the group or send the reply, message one person in it privately and tell them plainly you felt left out. Most people answer that kind of message kindly.

rising.upright:
'Right, pub.' Somebody says it at the end of the meeting and half the room follows, and with Aries rising it's usually you. You walk in already moving, and people read you as direct, quick and up for it. With the Three of Cups drawn for your mask, that energy is being taken as an invitation. Mercury has no standing of its own in Aries and borrows its manner from Mars, so your social talk is fast, teasing and fairly blunt. Most people like it. A few find it a lot.

The square between Cancer and Aries is where it rubs. The card wants warmth and a bit of lingering, introductions done properly, the long toast. Aries rising wants to get to the good part. From your side it can feel like doing everyone a favour, cutting through the awkward first twenty minutes so the fun can start, and often that's exactly what you're doing. What you might miss is the quieter person who needed those twenty minutes, and who went home early without you noticing.

In a new job this is organising Friday drinks in week two and being known for it by week three. At a party it's introducing two people who turn out to get on, and taking a quiet pride in it. In a sports team or an evening class it's being the one who ends up with everyone's number. It's worth asking whether any of the people you round up know much about you. Next time, ask one of them to organise it, and see what it's like to be the one invited.
rising.reversed:
Competitive is how Aries rising can come across with this card reversed, which is usually the last thing you mean. The quick joke lands as a jab. Somebody's story gets topped. You join a new group with a lot of energy and drift off within a month, and people read that as not caring. Mercury picks up Mars's edge in your sign, so first contact with a group starts to feel like a contest, and the others can tell.

At the office it's the colleague who hasn't warmed to you since the first meeting, where you talked over them. In a new friendship group it's being liked and slightly braced for. At the next gathering, stay an hour past the point you'd normally leave. Talk to the person who's said least, and let them finish every sentence.

sun.upright:
Look at the ground under the three women on this card. It's covered in fruit and gourds, the harvest in, and they've stopped work to drink to it. A Taurus Sun gets that picture straight away. You're here to build something solid and enjoy it, and to be known as someone whose table is worth sitting at. Cancer is sextile to Taurus, an easy link between two signs that get on, though a sextile is an opening you still have to walk through. Water and earth feed each other, and what grows between them grows slowly and lasts.

Mercury in your sign answers to Venus, so the card's talk turns sensual and unhurried. Long lunches, a good bottle, catching up properly. There's a less obvious thread too. Mercury's own slice of Taurus is its first ten degrees, the decan of the Five of Pentacles, the card of being left out in the cold. So there's an old Taurus worry about going without, about being the one on the outside, and the full table is partly your answer to it. That's fine. It does mean you can hold on to the same small circle for years and feel quietly threatened when it changes.

With money this is the generous host, the one who always brings more than was asked and privately minds the cost. Professionally it's the colleagues you've known for ten years and trust completely, and the new starter nobody's thought to take to lunch. At home it's the dinner that's been the same four friends for so long nobody asks anyone new. Ask someone new. One person, to the table you usually keep for the old crowd, and watch how the others take to them.
sun.reversed:
Taurus is the sign most likely to overdo this card, and it usually knows it. Reversed on your Sun, the celebrating gets heavy. Too much food, too much wine, another long lunch that leaves everyone flat by Monday. Venus rules your sign and Mercury follows her lead here, so pleasure does most of the talking. The other version is stubborn loyalty to a circle that stopped feeding you a while back, where you keep turning up out of habit and pride won't let you say it's gone stale.

The bank statement tends to notice first, then your body, then the friend who's been quietly declining invitations. There can be some hoarding in it too, the good bottle kept for an occasion that never comes. Host something that isn't built around eating. A walk, a working bee in someone's garden, an early swim. See who comes.

moon.upright:
Food, sleep, warmth, the same faces at the same table. That's how a Taurus Moon calms down, through the body first. This card is one you'd happily live inside. Earth and water are friendly elements, each giving the other shape, and Cancer sits sextile to Taurus, so the comfort on offer here is the sort you can take in without fuss. Mercury in Taurus goes along with Venus, which means your feelings tend to come out through what you do for people before they come out in words.

That's the tension, if there is one. The card belongs to Mercury, and Mercury wants the feeling said, ideally around a table with friends who'll hear it. You'd sooner cook for them. When you're upset you go quiet and practical and a bit stubborn, and you don't expect anyone to notice, and then you're hurt when nobody does. A long lunch with two old friends does more for you than a heart-to-heart. The heart-to-heart still has to happen now and then, and it's easier once the plates are cleared and nobody's rushing off.

Your body gets a lot out of company here. Meals eaten slowly with people you like, a hug that goes on a bit, a Sunday afternoon at a friend's place doing very little. With a partner it's the small rituals, the Friday takeaway, the walk after dinner, that tell you you're safe. With a friend of fifteen years it's being able to sit in silence and have it mean something. Who gets to see you when you're not okay? If the answer is nobody, tell one of those old friends one true thing next time you're at their table.
moon.reversed:
Comfort that's gone off, that's the reversed card on a Taurus Moon. Eating and drinking with friends as a way of not feeling anything, or else going to ground at home and turning down every invitation because the couch is safer. Mercury has a foothold in Taurus through the Five of Pentacles decan, and it can drag up an old fear of being left outside. So a change to the friends' routine, the regular dinner cancelled or moved, can hit much harder than it should.

Your body shows it first, sluggish and overfed or short of sleep. Then a friendship shows it, where you've gone a bit sulky and fixed and the other person can't work out why. Tell the group you miss the old dinner and want it back. Put a date in everyone's diary yourself so it actually happens.

rising.upright:
People relax near a Taurus Ascendant. You come across as calm and pleasant and unlikely to make a scene, somebody whose kitchen would be nice to sit in. Drawn for your mask, the Three of Cups means that's how strangers are reading you, as good company, easy to be around, probably a decent cook. Cancer is sextile to Taurus, so the card and your rising sign cooperate. The sextile only pays off if you do something with it, though.

You're slow to warm and you know it. At a party you'll find one corner and one person and stay there, and you'd like people to come to you. Mercury in your sign follows Venus's taste, so your charm is physical, the bottle you bring, the way you dress, the fact that you remembered what they drink. That goes a long way. The card suggests a few people are ready to take you into their circle and are waiting for a sign that you'd like it. A Taurus Ascendant can look perfectly content on its own, and people don't want to intrude.

With new neighbours it's the wave over the fence that could easily become a drink. In the office it's the group who go for lunch on Thursdays and assume you'd prefer not to. At a gym class or a choir it's the familiar faces you've nodded at for months. Say yes to the next invitation from someone you don't know well, even if it's outside your usual week. Bring something. You're good at that part.
rising.reversed:
From outside, a Taurus Ascendant with this card reversed can look like a closed shop. You and your old friends, the same table, the same in-jokes, and a newcomer can feel it the moment they sit down. You probably don't mean it. Fixed earth just gets settled, and Mercury in Venus's sign makes you pleasant enough that nobody says anything. The other version is the lazy host, lovely company when people come to you and no effort ever made the other way.

At work it shows as being seen as part of a clique you didn't know you were in. Socially it's invitations you never return. Go first for once. Introduce yourself to the new person, ask them along, and make the plan yourself, the time and the place and the booking.

sun.upright:
Mercury rules Gemini, so when a Mercury card turns up for a Gemini Sun it comes with the landlord's keys. This card is your own planet visiting the sign next door, Cancer, and that's worth thinking about. Neighbouring signs have little in common, each holding what the other lacks. You bring the talk, the news, the forty friends. Cancer brings the three who'd come round at two in the morning. What you get is your planet doing its usual thing in a warmer and more loyal key.

What you're building of yourself is a person who knows everyone and has something interesting to say to each of them, and fair enough, you're good at it. The card asks a slightly awkward question, which is which of those conversations actually feeds you. Air and water don't clash and don't mix on their own, so feeling has to be brought into the chatter on purpose. You'll know the difference when you feel it. There's the party where you worked the room brilliantly and came home empty, and there's the kitchen at the end of the night with two old friends, where you said something true and felt ten years younger.

In your job it's the whole network set against the two colleagues you'd actually trust with a secret. With a brother or sister, or a cousin who's more like one, it's years of talking every day and the one conversation you've never had. Online it's hundreds of contacts and a birthday post with a lot of likes. For your next bit of good news, skip the big drinks and have three people round. Choose them carefully, cook, and let the talk go wherever it goes.
sun.reversed:
The reversed card brings out Gemini's least lovely habit, and you probably know which one I mean. Gossip. With Mercury ruling your sign, news is a kind of money for you, and reversed, the Three of Cups spends it on belonging. You're in every group chat and fully part of none. A story told in confidence gets passed on because it was too good to keep, and you tell yourself it did no harm.

It tends to surface as a friendship that's cooled for reasons you can't pin down, or a colleague who's stopped telling you things. Sometimes it's the reverse, hearing what was said about you in a group you thought you were central to. Next time someone hands you a bit of news about somebody else, let it stop with you. Notice how often that comes up over a month.

moon.upright:
Talking is how a Gemini Moon gets over things. Anything, to anyone, though a friend who talks back fast is best. Mercury is the landlord of your sign, and this card is Mercury in Cancer, so this is your own way of coping taken somewhere a little deeper. The card wants the chat to reach the feeling. Air and water are neutral to each other, which in practice means they have to be introduced, since they won't meet by accident.

You can be very funny about your own troubles. That's one of your best qualities and it gets you through a lot. What happens, though, is that the funny version becomes the version. Friends laugh and move on, and the part that actually hurt never quite gets said. With this card on your Moon, the people around you are readier than usual to hear the sentence under the joke. You'll feel it when it happens. Somebody stops laughing and asks, and you find you want to tell them.

The group chat is where a lot of this lives, the late messages, the voice notes, the three friends who know everything. Siblings matter here too, or the cousin you grew up with, somebody who remembers you at nine. Watch your sleep, because after a really good night out your mind can stay lit until three. Next time a friend asks how you are, give them the answer you'd give if they weren't going to laugh.
moon.reversed:
For a Gemini Moon, this one can feel like a low hum of being left out. A message not answered, a plan made in a chat you weren't in, a photo you saw after the fact. Mercury is strong in its own sign, and reversed on your Moon it turns that strength into checking. Who's online, who's replied, what that short answer meant. You end up talking to everybody about everything except the thing that's actually bothering you.

Sleep goes first, the phone in bed and the scroll at two. Friends get a slightly anxious version of you, chattier than usual and oddly hard to reach. Mute the busiest group for a day. Ring one friend instead of messaging, and tell them the real reason you've been a bit off.

rising.upright:
Within ten minutes of arriving somewhere, Gemini rising has found out what everyone does and who knows whom. Mercury rules your Ascendant, which makes it your chart ruler, and the card you've drawn is Mercury's card for Cancer, so it sharpens how you come across. People are meeting you as the connector, the one who knows someone they ought to meet and will introduce them before the night's out.

You're good at this and you enjoy it. The buzz of a new person, the story you can file away, the moment two people you introduced start laughing together. Cancer is the sign next door to Gemini, and neighbours in the zodiac don't share much, so the warmth this card offers isn't your first language. It's a second one you can learn. What people don't always notice is that they think they know you after five minutes of good conversation. They've heard a lot of stories and none of them were about you.

In a new job it's being on first-name terms with the whole floor inside a week. At a wedding it's the table you end up at by accident, and the friend you make there. Online it's plenty of warmth in the comments and not much in the private messages. Who, out of everyone you've met lately, would you like to see again on purpose? Tell them, and tell them it was them you meant.
rising.reversed:
Gemini rising reversed can come across as flaky. You say 'we must catch up' to everyone you meet, and people start to notice that nobody ever does. Double bookings, a lovely chat with someone whose name you've lost by morning, a funny story repeated to the one person it was about. Mercury at home in your chart is quick and generous with words, and the words get spent without much behind them. It isn't dishonesty. Everything just sounds like a plan when you say it.

A new colleague stops taking your 'let's grab a coffee' seriously. At a party you're remembered as great fun, and nobody has your number. Only say 'we must catch up' when you've got a day in mind. Then say the day in the same breath.

sun.upright:
This is one of Cancer's own cards. The Three of Cups belongs to the middle ten degrees of your sign, where Mercury rules, so for a Cancer Sun it's speaking your language exactly. You're here to make a home and look after the people in it, and to be known as the one who holds everything together. Card and sign are both water, which turns everything up, the good and the too-much. Mercury has no special dignity in Cancer and takes its lead from the Moon, so the words come out of feeling and memory.

Cancer's Major is The Chariot, who goes out in armour, and this card is your sign with the armour off. That's lovely, and it's also hard for you, because you're usually the one running the celebration and very rarely the one being celebrated. You remember everybody's birthday. You bring the cake to work, you organise the card, you ring your aunt on the anniversary. Having it turned round on you, being fussed over, feels exposing, and you'll find a way to be busy in the kitchen all through your own party.

With family it's the long table at the gathering, and you making sure everyone's got a plate. With old friends, the school ones or the uni ones, it's the reunion you keep meaning to organise and the relief when someone else does. On the job it's the warmth you bring to a team and the thanks you wave off. Let someone else host your next birthday. Sit down, stay sat down, and let them get it slightly wrong.
sun.reversed:
When the Three of Cups turns over for a Cancer Sun, the family circle can close. The in-jokes go private, the new partner or new friend stays on the outside, and there's a quiet sense of who's really one of us. Mercury working for the Moon remembers every slight. Or it's too much of the caring, parties thrown for everyone else and nothing for you, and a resentment building that you'd be ashamed to say out loud.

The family is the usual place, and sometimes an old friendship group that's become hard for anyone new to join. Nostalgia can play a part, the old crowd missed so much that the present one never gets a look in. Tell one friend what you'd actually like for yourself, a thing, a day, some help. Be specific, and let them do it.

moon.upright:
The good news isn't quite real to a Cancer Moon until it's been told to someone. Your mum, your oldest friend, whoever that is for you. The Moon rules this sign, so the need to feel safe and fed and surrounded by your own runs deep. This card is native here, one of the three cards that belong to Cancer, and Mercury in the middle of your sign answers to the Moon. So this draw speaks straight to how you feel.

Card and sign share an element, and water on water turns things up. It's warm and easy among your people, and it's also easy to take on everyone's mood in a room and carry some of it home. Mercury here is memory with a voice. Old stories get told again, the holiday when you were eight, the dog, the time the car broke down on the way to the coast, and every retelling is a comfort. That's real nourishment for you. The catch is that a friend's bad week can become your bad week without anybody asking you to take it on.

Within the family it's the Sunday phone call, the recipe you still make, the group chat with your siblings. Among friends it's the ones who've known you longest. Your stomach is often the honest one, tight when a gathering's gone wrong and settled after a good long dinner. Ring the old friend you've been meaning to ring, and ask about the time you both remember.
moon.reversed:
Few placements feel left out as sharply as a Cancer Moon. With this card reversed the old hurt comes up, the party you weren't asked to at twelve, the cousin who was always the favourite, and a small thing now wakes the whole memory. Mercury in your sign, working for the Moon, can replay what was said until it's far bigger than it was. Or you go back into your shell and wait to be noticed, and sulk when you aren't.

Family gatherings are the usual place, and old friendships that have drifted. Comfort food and a second bottle with friends can creep in too. Say the plain thing to the person it's about. 'I felt left out' is enough. You don't have to explain the history behind it.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising tends to arrive a little shy. Kind face, watchful, taking the temperature of the room before you commit to it. The Three of Cups drawn here puts your Ascendant's own decan card on it, since this card belongs to the middle of Cancer, and so strangers are meeting the softest, most sociable version of you. You make people feel at home, often without saying much.

Your way in is small groups. At a big party you'll find two people near the snacks, and by the end of the evening you know about their mothers. Mercury in your rising sign follows the Moon, and what it gives you is a memory for people's details, names, children, what they were worried about last time. Same element, though, and water on water can tip into mothering strangers, topping up drinks, checking on the one who looks lost, and having no time for yourself at your own night out.

In a new job it's being the person people bring their problems to inside a fortnight. At a party in someone's kitchen it's being handed a job and feeling relieved. Meeting a partner's family, it's being liked by the grandmother straight away. Your shell is lower than usual with this draw. You might as well let someone see what's behind it, and tell them something about yourself for a change.
rising.reversed:
With the card reversed, Cancer rising puts the shell back on. To newcomers you can look cool or cliquey, warm to old friends and merely polite to everyone else, and people take it personally when it's really nerves. The Moon rules your Ascendant and Mercury follows her moods here, so your first impressions change with how you feel that day. Some days you're lovely at the door and other days you're barely there.

It shows at work as the new starter who decides you don't like them. At a gathering it's staying with your own people all night and missing someone who'd have been worth meeting. Pick one person you don't know at the next thing you go to. Ask them where they're from, and then one question after that.

sun.upright:
Nobody's in the middle of the circle on this card. The three women face each other, cups up, and none of them is the star, and a Leo Sun tends to notice that. You're here to be seen and loved for exactly who you are, and to be generous about it. It's a party card, and you do love a party. Underneath, though, Cancer and Leo sit side by side in the zodiac, neighbours with little in common, and the card is water while you're fire. That's steam, or one putting the other out.

Mercury is only a visitor in Leo and gets lit up by the Sun there, which makes the card's talk warm, big and generous. You'll give a brilliant toast. And somewhere in it there's a small flicker of wanting the toast to be about you, and you're a bit ashamed of the flicker, which you needn't be, because most people feel it. What the card asks is that you let someone else be the one lit up for a night, and put your own warmth into making sure they are.

At work this could be the colleague whose promotion you celebrate properly, with a speech and a decent card, and mean it. With children, yours or a niece or a godson, it's their school play and you in the audience for once. In a creative group it's the project that works because three people wrote it. Pick someone who deserves a fuss and make one for them. Let it be their night from start to finish.
sun.reversed:
Upside down on a Leo Sun, this card turns the celebration into a show. You're the host who needs the applause, the one telling the story at dinner when it was meant to be someone else's birthday. Or your pride gets hurt when you're off the centre, and you go quietly cool on friends who didn't make enough of your news. The Sun colours Mercury in your sign, and reversed that makes for a lot of talking with not much listening.

Money can come into it, the big gesture you couldn't really afford, the round bought so you'd be seen buying it. Friendships show it too, especially the one friend who's started to seem a bit tired of you. Ask that friend how they are. Keep asking, and save your own news for another day.

moon.upright:
Warmth, and being appreciated, is what a Leo Moon runs on, far more than it will ever ask for out loud. Drawn for your tides, this card is a lovely one in one sense, friends making a fuss of you and a bit of fun. It isn't a simple fit, though. Water and fire pull against each other, and Cancer's way of feeling is soft and private where Leo's is big, generous and a bit theatrical.

Mercury in Leo borrows the Sun's colour, so when you talk about how you feel you do it with force. The trouble is pride. You're loyal, you show up for everyone, you remember their big days, and when you're the one who needs cheering up you'd honestly sooner wait for someone to notice. They often don't, because you look so bright. That's quietly crushing, and you won't say so, and the not saying makes it worse.

Among friends, this card suggests a few of them want to make a fuss of you and are waiting to be let in. In love it's the affection that settles you, a compliment, being chosen in front of other people. Your body picks up on it more than you'd expect, a heaviness when you've felt overlooked and a real lift after a warm evening. Tell a friend you've had a hard time lately and you'd love a night out. Let them arrange it.
moon.reversed:
The forgotten birthday is the classic here. A Leo Moon with this card reversed takes being overlooked very hard, even when it's small and nobody meant anything by it. Mercury under the Sun's influence turns the hurt into a scene, or into a long, dignified silence that everyone can feel. Or you pile into the nights out to feel adored, and it works while you're there and goes flat in the taxi home.

Friends and partners get the brunt of it, usually as drama over something much smaller than the real hurt. Sleep goes late after the big nights. Next time you feel overlooked, say so to the person the same day, in one warm sentence, before it has time to grow.

rising.upright:
The room lights up a bit when Leo rising walks in, and you know it. With this card on the Ascendant, that's how people are reading you, as the life of the gathering, the one who makes the night. Mercury picks up the Sun's warmth in Leo, so your first-meeting talk is funny, generous with attention, and a little bit of a performance. People feel noticed by you, which is a real gift.

Cancer sits just behind Leo in the zodiac, and next-door signs don't share much. There's a softer, more private need behind your entrance that most people never see, and the card's water is where it lives. You do enjoy being the host, genuinely. After a night of being great company for everyone, though, you can go home oddly lonely, because nobody asked you anything. Fire and water are opposed elements, and the cost of keeping a room warm usually gets paid later, on your own.

At a party this is you introducing people and remembering everyone's drink. Starting a new job, you're known across the building within a week. On a first date it's being wonderful company and giving away nothing that matters. Somebody you meet soon is going to ask you a real question. Answer it properly, even if the answer's less shiny than your usual material.
rising.reversed:
Reversed, the big warm entrance can tip into too much. Too loud, too many stories, the host who's lovely and a bit exhausting. People might feel they're in an audience when they came for a chat. The other version is the VIP corner, you and your favourites at one end of the room and everyone else noticing it. With Leo rising this is rarely unkind in intent, and it still stings the ones left out.

At work it tends to show as a new colleague who finds you intimidating, and at parties as the quiet person who left early. Occasionally it's the opposite, you hiding behind the hosting because being a guest feels exposed. Go to the next thing as a guest and nothing else. Bring a bottle, sit down, and let somebody else run it.

sun.upright:
For a Virgo Sun this is a card from the landlord of your own sign. Mercury rules Virgo and is exalted there as well, which puts it at full strength, and the Three of Cups shows that same planet in a warmer mood, visiting Cancer. You want to be useful and known as someone who gets things right. Cancer and Virgo are sextile, and water and earth give each other shape, so the easy link is there. You still have to use it.

What gets in the way is that you tend to work at the party. You'll organise the celebration beautifully, spreadsheet and all, and then spend it checking the food's out and washing glasses. It is your way in, and it feels natural, yet the card shows three people who've put their jobs down. Mercury also rules the last ten degrees of Virgo, the Ten of Pentacles decan, the card of family and what gets handed down, so for some Virgo Suns this is specifically about family. The christening, the anniversary lunch, the long table at your parents' place.

At work this is the team you've carried and never celebrated with. With family it's the gathering where you'll be the one who remembered everything and the last to sit down. With your own body it's the habit of running on nerves and coffee around other people and crashing afterwards. At the next celebration, give yourself one job and one only. Do it, then find a chair and keep it for the rest of the night.
sun.reversed:
The critic comes out when this card reverses on a Virgo Sun. You're at the dinner and you've noticed the undercooked potatoes, the friend who talks too much, the flaw in the toast, and some of that gets said on the drive home. Mercury is very strong in your sign, and upside down it turns its precision on the group. It can pass for gossip with better grammar. The other version is overwork as a hiding place, too busy to come out, again.

Easy-going friends feel it first. Colleagues feel it at the work do you left early. Go to the next thing and keep every judgement to yourself for the whole evening. Afterwards, write down one thing you actually enjoyed about it, and send that to whoever organised it.

moon.upright:
Being useful settles a Virgo Moon. A routine to follow, a small job to do for someone, a problem sorted. Mercury rules Virgo and is exalted there, so the card's planet is completely at home in your emotional life. You process feelings by talking them through precisely, sorting what happened into what it meant. The Three of Cups asks you to do that with friends, over a drink, and let them do some of the sorting for you.

Cancer is sextile to Virgo and the elements are friendly, so this is a gentle draw. The friction is mostly inside you. You tend to be a bit anxious at gatherings, watching whether everyone's all right, and replaying afterwards what you said to whom. Being cared for can feel like being a burden. Someone bringing you a cup of tea without being asked can make you want to cry, and then you'll tidy something so nobody sees.

Your body keeps close score here. A knotted stomach before a social thing, a looser one after a good evening with people you trust. With friends it's the two or three you can be a bit of a mess in front of. The Ten of Pentacles decan, Mercury's slice at the end of Virgo, brings family into it too, a parent or a grandparent's house where you still feel looked after. Let one friend look after you properly, dinner cooked and dishes done, without you lifting a finger.
moon.reversed:
The replay is what this looks like for a Virgo Moon. You come home from a perfectly nice evening and go over every word, what you said to your friend's partner, whether that joke was all right, why someone left early. Mercury is strong in your sign, and turned against you it becomes an anxious editor. The gathering starts to feel like an exam, so you go to fewer of them.

Sleep takes the hit, and so does your digestion, the body keeping its own tally of the worry. A friendship can cool because you've assumed they're annoyed with you and pulled back first. Check. Send the friend a light message about something else entirely and see how they answer. Usually it's warm.

rising.upright:
The ice, the bottle opener, the seating plan so nobody gets stuck next to the bore. Virgo rising is the one who thought of all that. You come across modest, neat and observant, and with this card on your mask people meet you as the person who makes a gathering work. Mercury rules your Ascendant and is exalted in your sign, so your chart ruler is the card's own planet at its most capable.

Helping is how you get into a room, and there's no shame in it. You're a bit shy underneath, and a task gives you somewhere to put your hands and a reason to talk to people. Cancer and Virgo are sextile, so the card's warmth and your practical manner work together here. What strangers pick up on is that you're kind. The risk is that they only ever meet the useful version, and never find out you're funny and quite sharp once you relax.

At a work do it's being the one who organised the leaving card and got everyone to sign. At a friend's wedding it's helping the caterers and missing the speeches. In a new club or class it's becoming the unofficial secretary by week three. Go to the next thing with no job at all. Stand somewhere central and talk to whoever comes.
rising.reversed:
Virgo rising reversed can come across as aloof, even judgemental, when mostly you're nervous. The careful manner reads as disapproval. You hover near the edge of the group, or you hide in the kitchen doing dishes nobody asked you to do, and people assume you'd rather not be there. Mercury, strong on your Ascendant, notices everything, and some of that noticing shows on your face. Your chart ruler is doing its job a little too well.

A colleague decides after one meeting that you're critical of them. At a party you get stuck on your own with the washing-up. Say something warm and a bit unguarded in the first five minutes of the next gathering. A compliment, a small admission, a laugh at your own expense.

sun.upright:
On the face of it, the Three of Cups was made for a Libra Sun. All grace and good company, everyone getting on. You want things fair and lovely and you want to be liked for making it happen. The astrology is less easy than it looks, though. Cancer squares Libra. Both are cardinal signs, both want to start things, and the square is friction that forces some kind of choice. Mercury in Libra keeps Venus's manners, so your talk at a gathering is charming, diplomatic and very good at putting people at ease.

Count the figures on the card. Libra is the sign of two, the couple, the partnership, and this card has three. That's where the square bites. There's the pull between your partner and your friends, or between the loyal little circle Cancer wants and the fair, open door Libra wants, and you can spend a whole evening making sure both are happy. It's tiring. You're so good at hosting everyone that you're not always sure who your own people are.

In love it's the question of how much your partner fits into your friendships, and how much you've given up to make it work. In the office you're the colleague everyone confides in and nobody quite knows. With your social calendar it's saying yes to three things on one Saturday so nobody's hurt. Write down the three people you'd call if something went wrong. Spend a whole evening with just them.
sun.reversed:
With this card upside down, a Libra Sun gets caught in the middle. Two friends have fallen out and you're still having lunch with both. Your partner and your best friend don't get on and you've been ferrying messages between them for months. Venus lends Mercury her charm in your sign, and it makes you very good at saying the pleasant thing to each side and very tired by the end of it. Sometimes the triangle is in love, a third person the relationship keeps circling back to.

Your calendar shows it, crammed with obligations you took on to keep things nice. So does your sleep. Pick one of those triangles and step out of it. Tell each person, kindly, that you won't be passing things on any more.

moon.upright:
Peace in the house is what a Libra Moon needs, and more than that, it needs the people it loves to be getting on. Pleasant company, a nice room, someone to talk to at the end of the day. This card brings friends, warmth and a bit of celebrating, and you'll feel better for it straight away. Mercury in Libra has Venus's grace, so you talk about feelings with a light touch and you're good at hearing other people's.

Cancer is square to Libra, though, and air and water don't blend without some help, so the feeling in the room and the words about it need an introduction. For you that often means the evening goes beautifully and you never say the one thing that's bothering you, because it would spoil the mood. The square pushes on exactly that. You'll recognise the drive home after a lovely dinner, pleased and slightly hollow, with the thing still unsaid.

With friends it's being the peacekeeper, the one who smooths it over when the group chat gets tense. With a partner it's feeling calmer when you're out together with other people, and a bit flat when it's just the two of you. The body shows it as tension across the shoulders after a social thing that looked relaxed. Tell a good friend, over a drink, the thing that's been bothering you. Let it spoil the mood for ten minutes.
moon.reversed:
A reversed Three of Cups on a Libra Moon can mean you'd sooner be anywhere than on your own. You fill the evenings, say yes to everyone, and don't notice until later that you've been lonely in company for weeks. Or the group has a conflict in it, and you're so afraid of taking sides that you end up avoiding the lot of them. Venus rules your Moon's sign and hates a sour note, and that's the whole difficulty.

Friendships show it, often as being the go-between for two people who aren't speaking. With a partner it can be an odd need for friends to be around whenever you're together. Spend one evening alone on purpose, doing something you like. Notice what you feel when there's nobody to keep happy.

rising.upright:
Libra rising arrives graceful and easy to talk to, and people feel better around you within a few minutes. The Three of Cups on your Ascendant makes you the social host, the matchmaker, the person who seats the right people together. Mercury answers to Venus in your sign, so your talk at a first meeting is warm, flattering in a nice way, and quite careful.

Cancer and Libra are square, and here that friction is about whether the warmth goes all the way down. Strangers find you lovely. The card suggests a few of them would like to be actual friends, which means seeing you a bit less polished. From your side it feels risky to be anything short of pleasant with someone new. So you smooth over every awkward moment, laugh at every joke, agree a little more than you mean. That works well enough, and people can still sense they're being handled, however gently.

At a party it's introducing two people who turn out to be perfect for each other. A new job makes you everyone's favourite in the first month, consulted on very little. Meeting a partner's friends, it's winning the whole table over by dessert. Next time you meet someone you like, disagree with them about something small and see what happens. They'll usually like you more for it.
rising.reversed:
Libra rising with this card upside down can come across as a bit fake, even when you're entirely sincere. The smile's on, you're lovely to everyone, and people wonder what you really think of them. Triangles creep in as well, being friends with both sides of something and quietly carrying things across. Venus rules your Ascendant and Mercury follows her lead, which makes the charm easy to switch on and hard to switch off.

Colleagues compare notes and find you agreed with each of them. Socially it's the new friend who's heard you say something slightly different to someone else. Be a touch less agreeable at your next first meeting. Say what you'd honestly like to do, and let the other person decide whether they're in.

sun.upright:
Casual friendship isn't really a Scorpio thing. You want depth, loyalty and the truth, and you'd like to be known as the one people trust with it. The Three of Cups comes to you in your own element, water to water, and Cancer is trine to Scorpio, so this card flows into your sign without resistance. Mercury has no rank in Scorpio and goes along with Mars, or Pluto if you use the modern ruler, and so the talk goes straight past the small stuff.

Your circle is small, you chose it carefully, and you'd do almost anything for the people in it. What this card asks for is something you're less used to, which is celebrating with them. Lightly. Laughing about nothing. That can seem almost pointless to you, because what matters is what happens when things go wrong. The good times count too, and the people who've seen you through the bad ones would like to see you happy. Water on water amplifies everything, so the bonds here are intense, and it's worth noticing if any of them have tipped into possessive.

In your working life it's the two or three allies you'd trust with anything, and a win worth marking with them properly. In love it's your partner and your closest friend finally getting to know each other. With shared money it's the group holiday or the joint present, pooled trust. Book something purely for fun with your best people. Keep the conversation light the whole way through, if you can manage it.
sun.reversed:
Secrets in the group are the risk when this card reverses on a Scorpio Sun. Who said what to whom, who can be trusted, who's been talking. Mercury picks up Mars's sharpness in your sign, and reversed it goes looking for betrayal and sometimes finds it. You may be testing a friend's loyalty without telling them there's a test. Or there's been a falling-out and you've gone completely cold on someone you used to be close to.

The friend group usually shows it first, then love, where a third person makes you uneasy. Holding a grudge for years is a Scorpio skill and it costs you. Ask the friend you suspect a straight question. If the answer's reasonable, believe it, and let the matter drop.

moon.upright:
What a Scorpio Moon needs is to be able to tell someone the whole truth and have them stay. A Scorpio Moon can go years without that, and it wears on you more than you let on. Cancer is trine to Scorpio and both are water, so this card slips into your emotional life very easily. It's about the friends you can be completely honest with, and the relief of being known.

Mercury has no standing in Scorpio and borrows its intensity from Mars, and from Pluto in the modern reading. So you don't chat about feelings. You either say nothing or you say the entire thing in one go at one in the morning. With the right two or three people that's a gift. Two water signs amplify each other, which means the good nights are unforgettable and a bad night in the group can stay with you for weeks. Trust, with you, is slow to build and very hard to get back once it's gone.

Somewhere in your life there's a friend who knows your worst secret and has never told a soul. In the family there's the old unspoken thing, and the cousin who's finally the first to say it. Sleep can go deep and vivid after a big conversation. Often this shows up as a night that starts out light and ends with everyone round the table telling the truth. Stay for that part.
moon.reversed:
For a Scorpio Moon, jealousy is the thing to watch with this card upside down. A friend has a new friend, and you feel it in your chest. A partner laughs a bit too long at someone's joke. Mercury in your sign follows Mars, and it turns that feeling into theories, and you can brood on who said what for far longer than the thing deserved.

Friendships show it as a silence nobody understands, and love shows it as a third person who may be entirely innocent. Sleep gets restless. Tell the friend, plainly and without drama, that you've been feeling a bit left out. Most of the time they had no idea, and they'll be glad you said.

rising.upright:
People meeting Scorpio rising often sense a lot going on behind your eyes, and they're right. This card drawn for your mask softens that first impression. Cancer and Scorpio are trine, water to water, so the warmth comes through you without any strain, and strangers get to see the loyal, funny side of you sooner than they usually would.

Mercury in Scorpio takes its edge from Mars, and in a first meeting that makes you sharp and fairly direct, quick to get past the small talk. Some people love it. Others feel a bit exposed. What's different with this draw is that you're more willing to show you like someone. That's a real risk from where you're standing, because being open in a new group feels like handing over something you might want back. The shared element amplifies, so when you do let someone in, you let them all the way in.

At a new job this could be the colleague who becomes a real friend inside a month. At a party it's the conversation in the corner that goes on for three hours. With a partner's friends it's the moment they decide you're all right and start teasing you. Say yes the next time someone new asks you along. Go without checking first who else will be there.
rising.reversed:
This reversed card can make Scorpio rising look like a closed door. Your circle seems impossible to join, and newcomers can feel they're being assessed from across the room. Mars sharpens Mercury in your sign, so a short answer can come out harder than you meant it. Sometimes you're protecting people you love from someone you've decided not to trust, and the person being kept out can feel it.

At work it shows as the team who've formed their own group without you, or the new person who's frightened of you for no good reason. Socially it's the friend of a friend you never warmed to. At the next gathering, go over to someone who's on their own. Ask how they know everyone, and actually listen to the answer.

sun.upright:
Birthdays are where it shows. A Sagittarius Sun has friends in three countries and a vague idea of when any of them was born. You want room to roam and something to believe in, and to be known as the one with the best stories. You love a party, so this card ought to suit you, and the astrology makes it awkward. Mercury is in detriment in Sagittarius, the sign opposite its home, so it's working against the grain. Cancer is quincunx to your sign, five signs apart, with nothing in common. Water on fire doesn't help either.

This card is about small, close, remembered things. In-jokes, anniversaries, the friend you've had since you were six. You're wonderful company, you love your friends, and you're a bit hopeless at keeping in touch. It doesn't feel like neglect to you. It feels like life moving fast. Mercury does have a foothold in your sign, though. It rules the opening decan of Sagittarius, the Eight of Wands, the card of messages flying through the air, and when you use that, one voice note can keep a friendship going for a year.

When you travel, it's the friends you met in a hostel twelve years ago and still see. From work there's the colleague who became a mate on a conference trip and hasn't heard from you since. The family reunion keeps happening without you because you're somewhere else. Pick the three friends you'd hate to lose and put their birthdays in your phone with a reminder. Ring on the day, wherever you are.
sun.reversed:
Reversed, a Sagittarius Sun can overdo this card in the most Jupiter way possible. The party that runs all weekend, the round that turns into six, the toast that says something tactless about the bride's ex. Mercury is in detriment in your sign, and upside down it speaks before it's checked the room. The other version is flaking, always somewhere else when the reunion happens, always promising to come next time.

Friendships notice both. So does your body after the big nights, and your bank account after the big trips with the big crowd. Pick one gathering you'd normally skip or overdo. Go early, drink less than everyone, and leave while you're still enjoying it. People will remember you were there, and you'll remember it too.

moon.upright:
Room to move, a laugh, and something to look forward to. A Sagittarius Moon gets restless the minute life gets small. This card gives you the laughing part, friends and fun and a bit of silliness, and you'll feel lifted by it. Mercury is in its detriment in your sign, which matters for how you handle feelings. Mercury's way is to name them and sort them. Yours is to feel something hugely for an hour, find the meaning in it, and get going again.

Cancer sits quincunx to Sagittarius, and fire and water are opposed, so Cancer's way of being comforted doesn't fit yours easily. Cancer wants to be held and fed and talked through it. You'd sooner go for a walk with a mate and talk about anything else. When a friend tries to have the serious conversation it can feel like being cornered, and you'll crack a joke to get out of it. Sometimes that's healthy. Sometimes the joke is the only thing standing between you and some real comfort.

With friends it's the road trip where the best conversation happened in the car after dark. With a partner it's needing a bit of freedom even inside something close. Your body settles when it's moving, outdoors, with people. Plan something with a friend that involves going somewhere, a long walk or a day out. If the serious talk comes up on the way home, let it.
moon.reversed:
When the card's reversed, a Sagittarius Moon uses company to run from something. The next party, the next trip, the next big group dinner, anything but a quiet evening where the feeling might catch up. Mercury is weak in your sign, so finding words for what's wrong is hard, and you don't look. Or you tell a very funny story about a very bad week and let everyone laugh.

It turns up as tiredness after too many late nights, a partner who feels lonely even though the house is always full, and a friend who's noticed you never talk about anything real. Spend one evening in with one friend and no plan. Let it be a bit boring, and see what comes up.

rising.upright:
In a hostel, at a festival, on a group tour, Sagittarius rising is the one who's got everyone's name by lunchtime. You come across friendly, open and up for anything, and with this card on your mask people read you as the person who brings strangers together. Mercury rules the first decan of your sign, the Eight of Wands, and that's the speed of it, introductions that turn into plans inside an hour.

It's worth knowing, though, that the card's planet sits badly in Sagittarius. Detriment means it's working against the grain, and the careful, feeling way with words this card is about doesn't come naturally. You blurt. You say the funny thing that's slightly too honest, and mostly it lands, and sometimes it doesn't. With Cancer quincunx your sign and water against fire, there's a gap between the big friendly first impression and the quieter, closer warmth of the card. You've made twenty new friends in a week. Some of them are waiting to see whether you'll remember them.

Travelling, it's the group you fall in with and the promise to visit that you might actually keep. A new team loves you in the first month. At a wedding you're the guest everyone remembers on the dance floor. Pick one person from the last lot of new friends and follow up with a proper message, with a question in it about them.
rising.reversed:
The loud one at the table. That's the risk for Sagittarius rising when this card reverses. The big personality that's usually welcome comes across as too much, a joke about someone's partner, a story that goes on, an invitation thrown out to everyone that nobody takes seriously. Mercury in detriment in your sign speaks first and checks later. Or you move on so fast that the people you meet never get a second conversation.

In the office there's the new manager who wasn't charmed. Socially it's the friend of a friend who found you a bit much and said so afterwards. Bring the first meeting down a notch. Ask plenty of questions, and keep your best story for the second time you see them.

sun.upright:
Milestones tend to go unmarked with a Capricorn Sun. You want to build something that lasts and be respected for it, and the celebrations get skipped on the way. Cancer is opposite Capricorn in the zodiac, so this card comes from the other end of your own axis. Home and family at one end, career and standing at the other. An opposition is a pull toward balance, and this draw is pulling you back to the table.

Mercury in Capricorn falls in with Saturn, dry, careful and quite funny once you let it be. Earth and water get on, so there's no real fight between you and the card, just a habit. You hit the milestone and file it. The promotion, the paid-off loan, the degree finished at night. You mean to mark it, and then there's the next thing. It doesn't feel like denial. It feels sensible. The people who helped you get there were probably waiting for a chance to say well done, though, and it never came.

At work this is taking the team out after the thing you delivered, and paying for it. There's a relative you only see at funerals, and a lunch you could have with them in between. With old friends it's the group you drifted from while you were busy climbing. Pick a milestone you've passed without marking and mark it, even late. Tell people why you're celebrating.
sun.reversed:
Friendship as networking is the risk for a Capricorn Sun with this card upside down. Drinks with people who'll be useful, the dinner that's really about the deal, a social life that's all strategy and no fun. Saturn's influence on Mercury in your sign turns cold when the card's upside down, and warmth becomes calculation. Or you've simply stopped going out, because work always wins, and your oldest friends have given up asking.

The Devil is Capricorn's Major, so be honest with yourself about any gathering you only get through with a few drinks in you. At work it shows as allies who don't feel like friends, and at home as a partner who's lonely on weeknights. Ring one old friend who can do nothing at all for your career. Book a night and keep it.

moon.upright:
Coping on its own is how a Capricorn Moon feels safe, that and being in control. This card asks for the opposite kind of comfort, being looked after, leaning on friends, letting people see you're not fine. Cancer is directly opposite Capricorn, and the card comes from the far end of your own axis. That opposition is a pull toward balance, and it can feel like being asked to do something you were never taught.

Saturn runs your sign and Mercury follows his lead there, so you talk about feelings drily and briefly, if at all. 'Bit of a week.' That's the whole report. Water and earth are on good terms, so the card isn't fighting you. It's offering something you actually need and find very hard to take. Being fussed over feels like a debt you'll have to repay, and you'd sooner cope. You're very good at coping, and it gets lonely.

There's usually a friend who always asks how you are, gets 'fine', and keeps asking anyway. With a parent it's the old family rule about not making a fuss. Your body carries it as tension in the jaw and shoulders, and sleep that doesn't quite restore you. Next time someone offers help, say yes before you've thought about it. Let them carry something, even something small.
moon.reversed:
The friend who never calls, that's often a Capricorn Moon with this card reversed. It isn't a lack of care. You're coping, you're busy, you'll ring when things calm down, and they never quite do. Saturn rules your sign, and with the card upside down Mercury can't find the words for what you need. Or they come out as criticism of the people who are trying to help.

It shows in friendships that have quietly thinned, and in a partner who feels shut out of your worries. Your body keeps the account, in the shoulders and at three in the morning. Message the friend who always reaches out first, and this time be the one who suggests a date.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising comes across reserved and capable, with a dry humour people only catch the second time they meet you. This card on your mask lets the warmth show sooner. Cancer sits opposite Capricorn, which puts it on your Descendant, the cusp of the seventh house, so the Three of Cups is coming at you from the people across the table. They're drawing you out, and you're letting them.

Mercury in your sign keeps Saturn's formality, so your talk at a first meeting is careful, a bit formal, and very good at sizing people up. Earth and water suit each other, so the card's softness doesn't fight your front. It just lets people see what's behind it. That can feel exposing. The work party where you actually laughed out loud, the new colleague who saw your eyes go at a leaving speech. People like you much more once they've seen that.

At work it's the office party where the junior staff realise you're human. With a partner's family it's the moment you stop being polite and start being funny. At the school gate it's the parents who'd assumed you were stiff, until one conversation about the traffic. In a new neighbourhood it's the street barbecue you nearly didn't go to. Go to the thing you'd usually skip for work reasons, and stay past the speeches.
rising.reversed:
Stiff at parties, the one in the corner talking shop. Capricorn rising reversed can come across that way when really you're unsure what to do with your hands. Or every social thing turns into networking, and the people you meet can feel they're being assessed for their usefulness. Saturn's formality stays on Mercury in your sign long past the point where it's needed. People would honestly like to know you, and the front makes it hard.

The team don't invite you to Friday drinks, assuming you'd say no. Socially it's a friend's partner who thinks you disapprove of them. At the next gathering, leave work out of it completely. Ask about someone's holiday, and tell them about yours.

sun.upright:
Aquarius Suns want to belong to something bigger than themselves and still be entirely their own person. You're friendly with nearly everyone and close to a few. The Three of Cups looks like your sort of card, friends and community, yet it comes from Cancer, the sign of family and the small loyal circle, and Cancer is quincunx to Aquarius. Five signs apart, very little shared, a lot of small adjusting.

Saturn rules your sign, with Uranus as the modern ruler, and Mercury picks up their coolness there, clever and interested in ideas. Air and water are neither friends nor enemies, so feeling has to be invited into your friendships deliberately. You care enormously about people in general and about your causes, and when a single friend wants you properly close, you can feel a bit trapped. Mercury has its own ten degrees in your sign too, the middle decan, the Six of Swords, the card of crossing the water to somewhere quieter. Some Aquarius Suns know that pattern well, drifting away from a group once it gets too intimate.

In a community group or a campaign it's being the organiser everyone respects and nobody really knows. On the job you're friendly with every department. With friends it's the two or three who've stuck with you through your phases and become family without anyone saying so. Tell one of them that's what they are. Say it in person.
sun.reversed:
Upside down for an Aquarius Sun, this card can mean the cause has taken the place of the friends. You're at every meeting and every march and you haven't seen your best friend in months. Mercury in your sign, cooled by Saturn, can get theoretical, fond of humanity and forgetful of a birthday. The other version is the scene, an in-crowd of clever people who all think alike, with everyone outside it treated as a bit dim.

It shows up as friends who feel they come after your projects, and a partner who'd like you home once in a while. Put a friend's thing ahead of a group thing, once, and tell them you did. It'll mean more to them than you'd expect.

moon.upright:
Ideas comfort an Aquarius Moon, and so does being understood. You need space to think, some distance, and friends who don't crowd you. This card is the Cancer end of friendship, warm and close, and Cancer is quincunx to your sign, so this fit takes a lot of small adjustments. Water and air have no natural ease together, and they have to be introduced on purpose.

Mercury in Aquarius borrows Saturn's reserve, and Uranus's detachment in the modern reading, so you tend to think your feelings before you feel them. You can explain exactly why you're sad, very clearly, in the voice of someone describing the weather in another city. Friends who care about you find that hard to get close to. Being fussed over can feel a bit like being caged. What this card says is that some of your friends are ready to be close without crowding you, and it's worth letting them.

With friends it's the late-night conversation about everything that turns, around two, into something personal. At home it's the need for your own evenings and the guilt that comes with it. The Six of Swords decan, Mercury's part of your sign, adds a habit of quietly moving on when a friendship gets heavy. Next time a friend asks how you really are, answer with a feeling first, and give the explanation after.
moon.reversed:
Everyone's laughing at the table and part of you is watching from the ceiling. That's what this card reversed can feel like for an Aquarius Moon, apart in the middle of a crowd. Mercury in your sign turns feeling into commentary, and upside down it can keep you up there, understanding everything and touched by none of it. Or you become the friend who's always there for everyone else and has nobody to ring.

It shows in a friendship group where you're central and oddly lonely, and in sleep that's full of thinking. A partner might say you're hard to reach even when you're sitting right beside them. Ring the friend you'd ring if you ever let yourself need someone. Tell them you're not doing that well.

rising.upright:
The dinner where nobody's quite like anybody else and everyone has a good time is very Aquarius rising, especially with this card on the mask. People meet you as the one who gathers the oddballs. You come across friendly, a bit unusual and slightly hard to pin down. Mercury in your rising sign answers to Saturn, and to Uranus in modern charts, so your first-meeting talk is clever, a bit off-beat, and genuinely curious about people's ideas.

Cancer is quincunx to your sign, and water and air need introducing, so the warmth this card offers isn't what strangers expect from you. That's partly why it works. People think you'll be cool and a little detached, and then you remember their dog's name. First meetings are easy for you on ideas and harder on feelings, and the move from interesting acquaintance to actual friend can be awkward. The card suggests a few people are waiting for you to make that move.

In a club, a community garden, a campaign, it's being the person who makes the new ones feel welcome. At work it's lunch with the colleague nobody else talks to. Online it's the friend you've only ever messaged. Suggest meeting the online friend in person. Pick a place with food and a proper table.
rising.reversed:
With the card upside down, Aquarius rising can seem aloof, part of the group and somehow above it. The outsider stance turns into a pose, and people feel they're being watched with interest when they wanted to be liked. The other way it goes is the in-group, a crowd of like-minded friends that's very hard for anyone ordinary to break into. Mercury, answering to Saturn here, can let the manner go cold without you noticing.

There's a colleague who's decided you think you're cleverer than them. Socially it's a friend of a friend who felt quietly judged. Next time you're at a party, find the most ordinary conversation in the room and join it. Take part properly, even if it's about property prices.

sun.upright:
Water meets water here, and the Three of Cups slides into a Pisces Sun without any friction at all. Cancer is trine to Pisces, the easy flow between signs of the same element. You want to feel connected to everything, to help, to make something beautiful and lose yourself in it. The harder part is Mercury, which is in both detriment and fall in Pisces, as far from home as it ever gets.

Mercury wants to put things into words and keep them separate. You know things by feeling them, and words often seem too small for the job. So the card's gift reaches you through the look across the room, the song everyone knows the words to, the evening where nobody says anything important and everybody goes home lighter. You'll know the relief of a group where you don't have to explain yourself. The shared element amplifies, too, so you soak up the mood of every room, and a sad friend can leave you sad for days.

In creative work it's the band, the choir, the art class, where making something with other people is its own comfort. In friendship it's the one person who gets you without words. With your body it's how tired you get after crowds, even happy ones. Say yes to making something with two or three others. Don't worry about what it turns out to be.
sun.reversed:
The escape hatch is what to watch for when a Pisces Sun draws this card reversed. The party as a way out, the drink that becomes three, the group you disappear into so you don't have to be yourself for a night. Mercury, badly placed in your sign, struggles to find words for what's wrong, so you blur it instead. Or you lose yourself in other people's troubles and call it friendship.

It shows up in your energy the day after, in a creative project that's stalled while you look after everyone, and in a friend who leans on you and never asks back. Say no to one rescue this month. Put that evening into your own work, alone, with the phone off.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon needs to feel connected, and then needs time alone to recover from it. Music, water, sleep and a few gentle people are what settle you. This card is water on water, and with Cancer trine Pisces its comfort pours straight in. You'll feel lifted by friends, the easy, forgiving ones who don't need you to be anything in particular.

Mercury is in detriment and fall in your sign, so its usual method of naming and sorting fails here. It has to learn your way of knowing, which is by feel, by mood, by dreams. For you, being comforted by friends often happens without talking about the problem at all. A night of laughing, a film on the couch with someone's head on your shoulder, a friend who texts you a song. The catch is that the same openness takes in everyone else's sadness too, and you may not notice until you're worn out.

With friends it's the two who can sit with you when you're low and not try to fix it. In the family it's the relative who shares your sense of humour and your tears. Sleep matters a lot here, deep after a good evening and broken after a sad one. Keep a quiet day free after any big gathering. Use it for nothing much.
moon.reversed:
A reversed Three of Cups on a Pisces Moon can mean soaking up the group's mood until you've lost your own. Everyone's sad, so you're sad. Everyone's drinking, so you're drinking. Mercury, as far from home as it gets in your sign, can't hold a line between their feelings and yours. Or you hide from people altogether, because every gathering costs too much, and then you feel the loneliness of that.

It shows in sleep, in a low, foggy tiredness, and in a friendship where you've been carrying someone for months. Before the next gathering, decide what time you'll leave and tell someone. Go home at that time, however it's going.

rising.upright:
Strangers tell Pisces rising their life stories, often within ten minutes. You come across gentle, a bit dreamy and very easy to talk to, and with the Three of Cups drawn for your mask that gets turned up. Cancer is trine to Pisces and both are water, so this card flows through your manner without effort, and people meet you as kind, warm and somehow already familiar.

Words aren't really how you make a first impression, which is just as well, since Mercury is in detriment and fall in Pisces. You make it with your face, the listening, the way you laugh. A new group can feel lovely and a bit overwhelming at once. You pick up the mood of the room quickly and you tend to match it. Two water signs together amplify, so on a good night you're everyone's favourite, and on a tense one you'll carry the tension home with you.

At a party it's being cornered in the kitchen by someone's divorce, and not really minding. In a new workplace it's the other new starter who comes to you with their worries in week one. In a creative group it's being the one who holds the mood together. Notice who you feel good around after a first meeting. Follow up with them, and let the others drift.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on a Pisces Ascendant, this card can make you seem vague and hard to pin down. You say yes to everything and turn up to half of it. You drift between groups and nobody's sure which one is yours. Mercury is weak in your sign and has trouble saying a clear no, so you say maybe and hope it sorts itself out. People aren't cross, exactly. They just stop counting on you, and you feel that.

Socially it shows as a reputation for being lovely and unreliable. On the job it's taking on other people's problems in your first month and running out of energy by the second. Give a clear answer to the next invitation, yes or no, within a day. Keep whichever answer you give.

1.upright:
The first house is you in person, the body and face you walk in with and the way you start things. Mercury has its joy here, the house where it does its best work, and this is a Mercury card, so the Three of Cups is well placed in the first. It makes your own presence a gathering point. People want to be near you, you're easy to talk to, and things start for you because somebody introduced you to somebody.

The friction comes from the sign underneath. Aries is the first house's natural sign, and Cancer is square to Aries, water against fire. Aries wants to begin alone and quickly. The card wants you to begin with company, the right people around you, and that can feel slower than you'd like. It's the difference between charging into something and turning up with two friends who've got your back. The second is usually the better start, even when it's less of a thrill.

With your body, it's the lift you get from moving with others, a walking group, a team, a class. With your appearance it's dressing for the people you'll be with, and enjoying it. With new starts it's the project you begin alongside a friend. Tell someone about the next thing before you begin it. Let them in on it early and see what they add.
1.reversed:
In the first house, the reversed card can mean losing yourself in the group. You start dressing for the crowd, laughing at jokes you don't find funny, agreeing with whatever the loudest person says. Mercury does well in this house, and upside down it gets very good at fitting in. The square from Cancer to Aries makes the other version sharp too, going off on your own in a sulk after feeling left out.

Your body shows it as tiredness after social things. Your decisions show it as waiting for friends' approval before you start anything. Find one choice you've been making to fit in with a group. Make it your own way instead, and don't explain it to anyone.

2.upright:
Actual money, what you own, and what you think you're worth. That's the second house, and with the Three of Cups in it, money and friendship get tangled up, mostly in a good way. Shared costs, a group present, earning through people you know. Cancer is sextile to Taurus, this house's natural sign, and earth and water nourish each other, so what grows here grows slowly and holds.

Venus is the natural ruler of the second, and the card brings Cancer's instinct to feed people. You'll likely find yourself being generous, picking up the dinner bill, lending the car, putting in for the present. That's good, and it's worth keeping an eye on where it goes. Self-worth comes into it as well. Feeling valued by your friends can make you feel richer than any pay rise, and feeling left out can knock your confidence about money in a way that doesn't quite make sense.

At work it's the collaboration that pays, a joint project, a referral from a friend. At home it's the shared kitty, the housemates' fund, the family pooling for something. With your possessions it's the thing you lent out and would quite like back. Spend a bit on bringing people together, a dinner or tickets to something, and set the amount before you start.
2.reversed:
With the card reversed in the second house, money and friends can get awkward. The group dinner where everyone splits the bill evenly and you only had a salad. The loan to a friend that's never been mentioned since. Spending to keep up with a crowd that earns a lot more than you do. Venus rules this house, and reversed the card can try to buy belonging with money you don't really have.

It shows up in your bank statement, and in a friendship where resentment has crept in over something small and financial. Ask for the money back, kindly, or decide clearly that it was a gift. Either way, say it out loud to them.

3.upright:
The third house is everyday talk, brothers and sisters, neighbours, short trips and whatever you're learning. Mercury is its natural ruler, so this card is on home turf. The Moon has its joy here as well, and the Moon rules Cancer, the card's sign, so both of the card's influences are comfortable in this house. It's one of the easiest places for the Three of Cups to land.

Gemini, the natural sign here, and Cancer are next door to each other and have little in common, and air and water need an introduction. In practice the chatter and the feeling have to meet on purpose. This is a house of group chats, catch-ups, the quick call to a sibling, and with this card those conversations get warmer. You'll notice people telling you real things in passing, on the phone while they're driving, in a message late at night.

With siblings, cousins and the family group chat, it's a good stretch for news and a laugh together. With neighbours it's the chat over the fence becoming a proper friendship. With learning it's a class or a course where the people end up mattering as much as the subject. Ring the sibling you usually only message. Talk about something from when you were kids.
3.reversed:
In the third house, the reversed card is gossip. A story goes round the family chat and lands on the wrong person. A message gets read in the wrong tone. A sibling hears something second-hand and it sits between you for months. Mercury is at home in this house, so words travel fast here, and reversed they travel before anyone's checked them. The Moon's joy is in this house too, which means feelings get into the talk quickly, and a careless line in a message can hurt much more than it was meant to.

It shows with brothers and sisters, with neighbours, with a class or a local group where you've been half-hearing things. When you hear something about someone, ask them directly or let it drop. Don't pass it on, even with the kindest intentions.

4.upright:
