The fourth house is home, family and your private ground, and its natural sign is Cancer. That makes this a card that belongs here. It's Cancer's own, water in a water house, and everything gets amplified, the warmth and the too-much alike. Home fills up. Family comes round, the table gets longer, somebody stays over, and the house can feel noisy and full in the best way.

The fourth is also an angular house, one of the four corners of the chart, which makes it active and visible, so what happens at home tends to matter a lot and get talked about. You'll feel the pull of your people, the urge to have everyone over, to cook, to hear the old stories again. The Moon rules this house, and with the card's Mercury answering to the Moon in Cancer, memory sits close to the surface. Somebody will get the photos out.

Within the family it's the gathering that heals something, or the relative who gets back in touch. With the house itself it's making room for people, the spare bed, the extra chairs, the bigger pot. With a parent it's a conversation where they tell you something about their own childhood you never knew. Have people round. Keep it simple, and ask the oldest person there to tell you a story.
4.reversed:
Family cliques are what this card reversed tends to point at in the fourth house. The siblings who side together, the in-law who's never quite included, the relative everyone talks about as soon as they leave the room. Same element, same sign as the house, so small hurts at home grow fast. Or there are simply too many people in the house, guests and visits and obligations, and nowhere left to be quiet. The Moon rules this house, and old family patterns come back without anyone deciding they should.

It shows around the kitchen table and in your sleep, which gets lighter when home's full. Include the one who's been left out, even in a small way. And keep one room, or one evening a week, that's only yours.

5.upright:
Play is what the fifth house is for. Romance, children, creativity, fun for its own sake. Venus has her joy here, and the Three of Cups is about as fifth-house as a card gets, friends laughing with a drink in hand. Cancer and Leo, the house's natural sign, sit side by side with little in common, and their elements are opposed, water to fire. So the play in this house has two moods.

Leo's fire wants to shine, show off a bit, have a big night. The card's water wants the fun to be close and familiar, with people who know you. You'll feel that as a question about what kind of fun you actually want. The best times here are probably the small ones, the dinner that ran late with three friends, the afternoon with the kids where nobody looked at a phone. Romance may come through friends, or a friendship may start to feel like something else.

With children it's their parties, their friends round, their small wins worth making a fuss over. With creativity it's making something with other people, a band, a play, a shared project. With love it's dates in a group and being introduced as someone's partner. Organise one night purely for fun, with nothing to achieve by the end of it.
5.reversed:
Too much is the risk with this card reversed in the fifth house. One more drink, one more late night, a weekend that leaves you wrecked. Or there's a third person in a romance, a flirtation that's gone further than it should, a friend who's a bit too close to your partner. Fire and water are opposed here, and upside down the fun either boils over or goes out. Venus has her joy in this house, and she doesn't love a limit.

It shows up in your energy and your wallet, and sometimes with children, a friendship between them that's gone sour and pulls the parents in. Pull the fun back to something you'll enjoy remembering. Keep the romance between the two people it belongs to.

6.upright:
What you actually do between waking and sleeping is sixth-house territory, the working day, the routine, the body's upkeep. Mercury is its natural ruler, so the card is on home turf here. Cancer is sextile to Virgo, the house's natural sign, and earth and water get on, so this is a comfortable placement. When this card lands in the sixth, the daily grind gets warmer. Colleagues turn into friends. The routine picks up some company.

Mars has its joy in the sixth, which gives this house some drive, and the card softens it. You'll notice it in how work goes, lunches together, a group who cover for each other, a team that laughs. That can make a dull job bearable and a good job a pleasure. Your body benefits too, from moving with others, eating with others, having someone to walk with. The upkeep that's hard to do alone gets much easier with somebody expecting you.

At work it's the colleague you start eating lunch with every day. With your health it's the exercise class you keep going back to because of the people there. With routine it's a shared habit, the walk with a neighbour, the swim with a friend. Find one part of your day you could do with someone else. Ask them if they'd like to join you.
6.reversed:
In the sixth house, the reversed card can mean the office clique. Lunches you're not invited to, a group chat about work you're not in, credit drifting towards the popular ones. Mercury rules this house, so the talk around a workplace runs fast and doesn't always run kind. Or it's too many late nights with colleagues and a body that's paying for them. Mars rejoices here, so friction at work gets physical quickly, tight shoulders and a short fuse by the afternoon.

It shows in how tired you are, in skipped meals and broken routines, and in how you feel walking in each morning. Get your basics back first, sleep and food and some movement. Then find one person at work you like, and build from there.

7.upright:
A partner, a business partner, anyone you've made a formal agreement with. That's the seventh house, the person opposite you. Drawn here, this card is about fitting that one-to-one bond into a wider circle. Friends meeting your partner, dinners with other couples, a business partnership that brings in a third person. Cancer squares Libra, the house's natural sign, and that friction forces something to move.

Venus rules this house and likes things balanced between two. The card brings in a third, and then some. Water and air need introducing, so the partnership and the wider circle have to be brought together with a bit of care. You'll feel it as questions about how much of your life to share with a partner, and how much of their world you want to be part of. Sometimes it's lovely. Sometimes one of you needs time with friends and the other takes it personally.

In love it's the dinner where your partner and your oldest friend finally click. In business it's a partnership that works best with other people around it, an adviser, a third partner, a community. With contracts it's an agreement made among friends, worth putting in writing all the same. Bring your partner into one of your circles and step into one of theirs. Watch how they are there.
7.reversed:
The classic third party turns up in the seventh house when this card is reversed. Sometimes it's a romantic threat, and more often it's just someone who takes up too much room. A friend who's always around, a parent with opinions, an ex who still texts. Venus rules this house and wants a balance of two, and the square from Cancer to Libra means there's friction to sort out. Nobody has to be the villain for this to hurt.

It shows up in arguments that seem to be about one thing and are really about who comes first. In business it's the partner who brings a friend into the decisions. Talk about it directly, the two of you, somewhere nobody else can hear.

8.upright:
The eighth house is what you share with other people at depth. Joint money, debts, inheritance, intimacy, and the endings that change you. Cancer is trine to Scorpio, the house's natural sign, and both are water, so this card goes into the eighth easily. Same element, and everything is turned up, which makes this house feel close and a bit intense.

Mars rules the eighth traditionally, Pluto in modern charts, and the card brings Mercury in Cancer's softness to it. So the depth gets spoken, among people who trust each other. The friend who tells you about their divorce, the family sorting out a parent's estate around the table, a partner who finally talks about money. It can feel heavy and also quite close, the sort of conversation that changes a friendship for good.

With shared money it's a joint purchase or a pooled fund that works because everyone's honest about it. With intimacy it's closeness that comes from talking and being known, and sex that's easier because the trust is there. With endings it's the wake or the farewell where people laugh as well as cry. Say the true thing to someone you share money or a bed with, and listen to theirs.
8.reversed:
The secret that leaks is what this card reversed points to in the eighth house. Something said in confidence gets around, or money shared with friends goes wrong, a debt, an unpaid share, a joint account one person's been dipping into. Jealousy can come in too, around intimacy, a third person who makes one of you uneasy. Water in a water house runs deep and fast, and Mars rules the eighth, so when it goes wrong it goes wrong with some heat.

It shows in shared money first, and then in trust. Get the money written down, who owes what and by when. And if you've been told a secret that's too heavy to carry, find a way to hand it back.

9.upright:
The ninth house is belief, study, long distance and whatever makes life mean something. The Sun has its joy here. Mercury, the card's planet, is in detriment in Sagittarius, the house's natural sign, so the card's close, familiar way of thinking has to stretch to fit a house that wants the big picture. Cancer is quincunx to Sagittarius and the elements are opposed, so the stretch is real.

In practice the card brings people into the ninth. Travel with friends, studying in a group, a faith or a philosophy you share with a community. You'll feel the tug between wanting to go far and wanting your people with you, and that's the friction. The best of it is probably a trip taken together, or a class where the conversations afterwards are as good as the lectures, or a wedding in another country where everyone you love is in one place for a few days.

With study it's the group you revise with, or the course you take with a friend. With travel it's the long trip to see someone who lives far away, or a group holiday. With belief it's the community that shares yours, or the friend who challenges it kindly. Plan one trip or one course with someone else, and share the planning with them from the start.
9.reversed:
In the ninth house, the reversed card is often the friend who moved overseas and slowly stopped writing. Distance did its work and neither of you meant it to. Or it's the group trip that turned into a week of arguments about where to eat, too many people with too many plans. Mercury is weak in this house's natural sign, and reversed it gets the tone wrong at a distance, the message misread, the call that keeps getting put off.

It shows in travel, in long-distance friendships, and in study groups where one person ends up doing all the work. Send the far-away friend something with some effort in it, a letter or a long voice note. Ask about their life over there.

10.upright:
Your public role, the job title, the reputation, what people say you do, all of it sits in the tenth house. Capricorn is its natural sign, and Cancer sits directly opposite Capricorn, so this card comes at the tenth from the other end of the axis, home against career. An opposition is a pull toward balance. The Three of Cups brings the warmth of home into the most public part of your chart.

Saturn rules this house and likes hierarchy and results, and the card is about people and celebration. Earth and water work well together, though, so the two can get on. Your career is likely to move through allies here, a mentor who puts your name forward, a team that wins together, a boss who's become a friend. It can feel strange to be rewarded for being liked. Your good relationships at work are a real asset, and it's fine to count them as one.

At work it's a launch or a team win worth marking properly. With your reputation it's being known as someone good to work with. With your family it's them turning up to see what you do, the show, the opening, the graduation. Throw the celebration for the team. Thank each person by name for the specific thing they did.
10.reversed:
Office politics are what the tenth house gets with this card reversed. The promotion that goes to the boss's friend, a reputation dented by gossip, a team split into camps. Saturn rules this house, and reversed the card turns professional friendships into alliances. Or your social life at work has become most of your job, and the actual work is slipping.

The opposition from Cancer can also bring family pressure about your career, a parent with strong views on what you should be doing. It shows up in your standing, and in your own sense of whether you belong where you are. Keep your work visible and your talk clean. Build one strong professional relationship on what you both do well.

11.upright:
The eleventh house is friends, groups, networks and the things you hope for. Jupiter has its joy here, so it's a lucky, generous house. The Three of Cups looks at home among friends, and in feel it is, yet the astrology is more complicated. Aquarius is the natural sign of the eleventh and Cancer is quincunx to it, five signs apart, with constant small adjustments to make.

Cancer wants the small, loyal circle, three people who know everything. Aquarius wants the wide network, the club, the movement. Water and air don't meet on their own and need introducing. You'll feel that as a question about which friends are which. A group you belong to might become more personal, or an old close friend might pull you into a bigger crowd. Often it's a nice surprise, the acquaintance who turns out to be a real friend.

In a club or a community group it's the people you start seeing outside it. Online it's the network that turns into a lunch. With your hopes it's a shared plan, something you want and a friend wants too, and working towards it together. Pick one person from a group you belong to and invite them to something just the two or three of you.
11.reversed:
A group you belonged to can re-form without you when this card reverses in the eleventh house. Or you realise you've outgrown a set of friends and don't know how to say so. Saturn rules this house, with Uranus in modern charts, and the quincunx with Cancer makes the adjustments uncomfortable. There's usually one friendship that's been drifting for a while.

It shows up in invitations that stop, a group chat that goes quiet, and a hope you'd shared with friends that's lost its energy. If the group has run its course, let it go. Keep the one or two people from it you'd miss, and tell them.

12.upright:
Behind the scenes is where the twelfth house works. Private life, retreat, sleep and dreams, the things you don't show. Pisces is its natural sign and Mercury is in detriment and fall there, so the card's usual way with words doesn't work well in this house. The Three of Cups has to find another way in. Cancer is trine to Pisces and both are water, so the feeling flows easily even when the words don't.

Saturn has its joy in the twelfth, which gives the house a quiet, solitary seriousness. With this card here, friendship happens out of sight. The friend who visits when you're unwell, the support group, the one person who knows what you're really going through. It can be comforting and a bit strange, being held by people who aren't on show. Same element, amplified, so these private bonds can mean a great deal.

With your sleep it's dreams full of old friends, sometimes people you haven't thought about in years. With a hard patch it's the friend who sits with you without needing to talk. With retreat it's a quiet weekend away with one or two people who don't need entertaining. Go and visit someone who's been out of circulation for a while. Take food, and stay a bit.
12.reversed:
In the twelfth house, the reversed card can be a friendship kept secret, or something kept secret from your friends. You've pulled back and haven't told anyone why. Mercury is at its weakest in this house's natural sign and can't find the words, so the distance just grows. Sometimes it's the drinking or the late nights that now happen alone, where company used to be. Saturn's joy is here, and solitude can harden into a habit without you noticing it happen.

It shows up in sleep, in a friend who's stopped hearing from you, and in a vague unease you can't name. Tell one friend, even briefly, what's been happening. You don't have to explain all of it.
